item.description:
FazerWM is a keyboard-driven tiling window manager for macOS.
- Windows tile into columns you drive from the keyboard: focus, move, resize, and reorder without touching the mouse. Vi- and Emacs-style keybind presets ship in the box. - Each display has its own workspaces, so different projects stay on different screens. Switch with a keystroke. Can be coupled in settings. - One keypress opens the overview: every workspace on every display at once, as thumbnails you can click to jump to. - Dragging works too. Labeled drop zones offer a new column or a stack, with more options under Pro. - Native macOS tab groups are managed as one window: they tile, move, and park together, and a column can hold tabs of its own. - Rules can send an app to a given workspace or column the moment it opens, matched by app, window title, or pattern. - Trackpad gestures and a recent-windows switcher sit alongside the keybinds. - Multi-display layouts survive a monitor going to sleep or reconnecting one screen at a time; columns and their order stay put. - A first-run wizard explains the two macOS permissions and what each one is for before asking for them. - FazerWM is free to use, tiling up to eight windows in a single workspace, and every install starts with a Pro trial. - Pro adds more workspaces and the fuller set of drag actions: drop as a tab, drag whole columns, pause at a display edge to switch workspaces mid-drag, or continue a drag inside the overview.

item.title: 2026.10.26-beta
item.description:
## What's new
- Pausing a window drag at a screen edge now moves between workspaces: left and right edges scroll the workspace a column at a time, top and bottom switch to the workspace above or below, and the bottom edge offers a new workspace when the last one is occupied. Parked-window thumbnails drag the same way, and with coupled workspaces every display switches together. A quick pass through an edge does nothing, so dragging between displays is unchanged. (Pro) - Pressing the overview key mid-drag continues the drag inside the overview, so a window can be dropped on any workspace, on any display. (Pro) - Dragging a thumbnail past the edge of an overview row now scrolls that row while the pointer rests on the band. The row keeps its scrolled position after the drop and springs back otherwise. - Drop zones have a new pill style with an icon and a label naming the action ("New column", "Stack above", "Add as tab"), and the edge bands have bolder indicators that stand out against window borders. - The Pro pane in Settings now lists the drag features included with Pro.
## Fixes
- Releasing a drag away from every drop zone after an edge switch now moves the window onto the workspace in view, instead of leaving it behind on the workspace it came from.
